records.source: וַיַּ֥עַל דָּוִ֖ד מִשָּׁ֑ם וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בִּמְצָד֥וֹת עֵֽין־גֶּֽדִי׃
records.gloss: And went up David from there and stayed in [the] strongholds of En-gedi.
pieces: David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En-gedi.

L.1: And David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En-gedi.

R.1: David left that place and went to live in the safe places in the hills at En-gedi.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: in the Hebrew text this sentence is 24:1
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. There chapter 23 ends at verse 28, and this sentence is counted as the first verse of chapter 24. Many Bibles print it as 23:29 and begin chapter 24 with the next sentence, so every verse of this chapter is one number lower there: 24:2-23 here is 24:1-22 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: the strongholds of En-gedi: hard-to-reach places in the hills by the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: En-gedi is a spring on the western shore of the Dead Sea, below steep cliffs full of caves (Joshua 15:62). "From there" is the wilderness of Maon, where Saul nearly caught David before a Philistine raid called him away (23:24-28). "Strongholds" are natural refuges in the rocks that a small band could hold, as in 23:14, 19.

decisions.choice: safe places in the hills
decisions.reason: Readable explains "strongholds" as places in the hills where David's band was safe, since the word here means natural refuges rather than built forts.

records.heading: David spares Saul in the cave

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁ֣ב שָׁא֔וּל מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֣ה דָוִ֔ד בְּמִדְבַּ֖ר עֵ֥ין גֶּֽדִי׃ס
records.gloss: And it was when returned Saul from after [the] Philistines, and they told him, saying, Look, David [is] in [the] wilderness of En-gedi.
pieces: When Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, word was brought to him: "David is in the wilderness of En-gedi."

L.2: And it happened, when Saul returned from [going] after the Philistines, that they told him, saying, "Look, David is in the wilderness of En-gedi."

R.2: Saul came back from fighting the Philistines. Then someone told him, "David is in the desert near En-gedi."

decisions.choice: verse numbers: many Bibles begin chapter 24 here
decisions.reason: Because the Hebrew text counts the previous sentence as 24:1 (see the note there), this verse is 24:2 here and 24:1 in many Bibles. Every verse to the end of the chapter is one number higher here than there.

decisions.choice: returned from after the Philistines: the raid of 23:27-28
decisions.reason: Saul had broken off his hunt for David to meet a Philistine raid on the land (23:27-28). Once that was dealt with, he turned back to David.

decisions.choice: they told him: an unnamed report
decisions.reason: The verb is plural with no named subject: people told Saul. As in 23:19, local informers kept Saul aware of where David was.

decisions.choice: word was brought to him (Balanced); someone told him (Readable); desert near En-gedi (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid an unclear "they". The "wilderness" is dry, rocky country with little rain, so Readable says "desert".

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח שָׁא֗וּל שְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֛ים אִ֥ישׁ בָּח֖וּר מִכָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ לְבַקֵּ֤שׁ אֶת־דָּוִד֙ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֔יו עַל־פְּנֵ֖י צוּרֵ֥י הַיְּעֵלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And took Saul three thousand men chosen from all Israel and went to seek David and his men on [the] face of [the] rocks of the wild goats.
pieces: So Saul took 3,000 men chosen from all Israel and set out to search for David and his men east of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.

L.3: And Saul took 3,000 chosen men from all Israel and went to seek David and his men on the face of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.

R.3: So Saul took 3,000 of the best soldiers in all Israel. He went to look for David and his men near the cliffs called the Rocks of the Wild Goats.

decisions.choice: chosen men: picked fighting men
decisions.reason: These are soldiers selected for skill, as in 26:2 and Judges 20:15-16. Saul had already kept such a band of 3,000 near him (13:2). The number is far larger than David's six hundred (23:13).

decisions.choice: Rocks of the Wild Goats: probably a local name for the cliffs
alternatives: the rocks of the wild goats (a description)
decisions.reason: The ibex, a wild mountain goat, still lives among the cliffs at En-gedi. The phrase may be a place name or a description, "the rocks where the wild goats are"; the sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: on the face of: in front of, facing, or to the east of
alternatives: on the face of the cliffs
decisions.reason: The expression can mean "in front of" or, since a person facing the sunrise has the east before him, "east of". It places the search near those cliffs without saying exactly where.

decisions.choice: east of
decisions.reason: Balanced takes the expression in its common sense of direction; Readable says only "near", which keeps the less certain point open.
Numbers above ninety-nine are given in figures at every level.

records.source: וַ֠יָּבֹא אֶל־גִּדְר֨וֹת הַצֹּ֤אן עַל־הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ וְשָׁ֣ם מְעָרָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֥א שָׁא֖וּל לְהָסֵ֣ךְ אֶת־רַגְלָ֑יו וְדָוִד֙ וַאֲנָשָׁ֔יו בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַמְּעָרָ֖ה יֹשְׁבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he came to [the] sheepfolds of the flock by the road, and there [was] a cave, and went in Saul to cover his feet. And David and his men [were] in [the] innermost parts of the cave sitting.
pieces: He came to the sheep pens along the road. A cave was there, and Saul went in to relieve himself, while David and his men sat far back in the cave.

L.4: And he came to the sheepfolds by the road, and a cave was there, and Saul went in to cover his feet. And David and his men were sitting in the innermost parts of the cave.

R.4: He came to some sheep pens beside the road. There was a cave there, and Saul went into it to relieve himself. David and his men were sitting deep inside that same cave.

decisions.choice: to cover his feet: to relieve himself
decisions.reason: This is a polite way of speaking about going to the toilet: a man squatting in a long robe covered his feet with it. The same expression is used of King Eglon in Judges 3:24. One ancient translation took it to mean that Saul went in to get ready or to rest, but the expression is the one used in Judges, and the story needs Saul to be alone, off guard and close enough for David to reach him.

decisions.choice: sheepfolds: stone pens for the flocks
decisions.reason: Shepherds built low stone walls, often at a cave mouth, to keep their flocks safe at night. Caves in these hills were used as shelters for sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: innermost parts: the far back of the cave
decisions.reason: The word means the farthest or deepest part of something (Judges 19:1; Amos 6:10). David's band sat in the dark at the back while Saul came into the lit entrance.

decisions.choice: to relieve himself
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture "to cover his feet"; Balanced and Readable give its meaning plainly, as at Judges 3:24, where the same words are used.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י דָוִ֜ד אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּ֨ה הַיּ֜וֹם אֲֽשֶׁר־אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֣ה אֵלֶ֗יךָ הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י נֹתֵ֤ן אֶת־אֹֽיִבְךָ֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר יִטַ֣ב בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֗ד וַיִּכְרֹ֛ת אֶת־כְּנַֽף־הַמְּעִ֥יל אֲשֶׁר־לְשָׁא֖וּל בַּלָּֽט׃
records.gloss: And said [the] men of David to him, Look, the day which said [the] LORD to you, Look, I [am] giving your enemy into your hand, and you will do to him as is good in your eyes. And arose David and cut off [the] corner of the robe which [belonged] to Saul in secret.
pieces: David's men said to him, "This is the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke of when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you, 'I am going to give your enemy into your hand, and you may do to him whatever you think best.'" Then David got up and quietly cut off the corner of Saul's robe.

L.5: And the men of David said to him, "Look, [this is] the day of which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to you, 'Look, I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as is good in your eyes.'" And David arose and cut off the corner of the robe that belonged to Saul secretly.

R.5: David's men whispered to him, "This is the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told you about! He said, 'I will hand your enemy over to you. You can do to him whatever you want.'" David got up and crept close. Without Saul noticing, he cut off a corner of Saul's robe.

decisions.choice: the day of which the LORD said: the men's reading of God's promises
alternatives: a promise given to David that is not recorded elsewhere
decisions.reason: No such word from the LORD is recorded in the earlier chapters. The men may be applying God's choice of David as king (16:1-13) and Jonathan's assurance (23:17) to this moment, or quoting a promise the writer has not told. Either way, they take the chance meeting as a sign that God means David to kill Saul; David's answer in verse 7 says otherwise.

decisions.choice: your enemy (singular)
decisions.reason: The written text can be read "your enemies", but the form the scribes marked to be read aloud is "your enemy", and the rest of the sentence speaks of one man ("do to him"). This translation follows the form read aloud.

decisions.choice: cut off the corner of the robe: an act that touches Saul's kingship
decisions.reason: The corner or hem of a robe could stand for its wearer's authority. When Saul tore the corner of Samuel's robe, Samuel said that the LORD had torn the kingdom from Saul (15:27-28). David's cut is a silent sign of the same thing, and it is why his conscience troubles him in verse 6.

decisions.choice: in secret: without Saul noticing
decisions.reason: The word means quietly or unnoticed (18:22; Ruth 3:7, where Ruth comes quietly to Boaz).

decisions.choice: whatever you think best (Balanced); whatever you want (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Good in your eyes" means what seems right to you. Readable adds "whispered" and "crept close", which the setting implies: the men are hiding in the cave with Saul at the entrance.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֔ן וַיַּ֥ךְ לֵב־דָּוִ֖ד אֹת֑וֹ עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרַ֔ת אֶת־כָּנָ֖ף אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְשָׁאֽוּל׃ס
records.gloss: And it was after thus, and struck [the] heart of David him because he had cut off [the] corner which [belonged] to Saul.
pieces: Afterward David's conscience troubled him because he had cut off the corner of Saul's robe.

L.6: And it happened afterward that David's heart struck him because he had cut off the corner that belonged to Saul.

R.6: But afterward David felt guilty for cutting off the corner of Saul's robe.

decisions.choice: his heart struck him: his conscience troubled him
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and conscience. The same words are used when David's heart strikes him after he counts the people (2 Samuel 24:10). Even this small act against the king felt to David like an attack on the man the LORD had chosen (verse 7).

decisions.choice: conscience
decisions.reason: Balanced says "conscience" for the heart in this sense; Readable says that David "felt guilty". Both add "robe", which the Hebrew leaves to be understood from verse 5.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו חָלִ֧ילָה לִּ֣י מֵֽיהוָ֗ה אִם־אֶעֱשֶׂה֩ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֨ר הַזֶּ֤ה לַֽאדֹנִי֙ לִמְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה לִשְׁלֹ֥חַ יָדִ֖י בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And he said to his men, Far be it to me from [the] LORD that I should do this thing to my lord, to [the] anointed of [the] LORD, to stretch out my hand against him, for [the] anointed of [the] LORD [is] he.
pieces: He told his men, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} forbid that I do this to my lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed, and raise my hand against him! He is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed."

L.7: And he said to his men, "Far be it from me, by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that I should do this thing to my lord, to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed, to stretch out my hand against him, for he is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed."

R.7: He said to his men, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} keep me from doing such a thing to my master! He is the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed. I must never attack him, because he is the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed."

decisions.choice: the LORD's anointed: the king whom the LORD chose and set apart by anointing
decisions.reason: Saul was anointed with oil by Samuel at the LORD's command (10:1), and the oil marked him as the LORD's own choice to rule. The phrase names the king by his relation to God: to raise a hand against him is to strike at the One who appointed him. David holds to this here, again in verse 11 and in 26:9-11, 23, and he treats the man who claims to have killed Saul as guilty for it (2 Samuel 1:14-16). The word is *mashiach*, "anointed one", the word that later became a title for the promised king (Psalm 2:2).

decisions.choice: far be it from me from the LORD: an oath-like refusal
decisions.reason: The first word is a strong exclamation, "profane!" or "unthinkable!" (Genesis 18:25). Adding "from the LORD" makes it a solemn refusal before God, close to "the LORD forbid" (26:11; 1 Kings 21:3).

decisions.choice: stretch out my hand against: attack, do harm to
decisions.reason: To stretch out the hand against someone is to attack them (22:17; 26:9).

decisions.choice: the king the LORD has anointed
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "the LORD's anointed". "Anointed" on its own is not an everyday word, and a reader may not know that it means the king, so Readable says "the king the LORD has anointed" each time the phrase comes in these books. This is the one wording used for the phrase throughout Samuel, Kings and Chronicles at Readable.

decisions.choice: the LORD forbid (Balanced); May the LORD keep me from (Readable); my master (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a familiar form of the oath-like refusal. Readable says "master" for "my lord", because David is speaking of the king he served, and "lord" could be confused with the LORD.

records.source: וַיְשַׁסַּ֨ע דָּוִ֤ד אֶת־אֲנָשָׁיו֙ בַּדְּבָרִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א נְתָנָ֖ם לָק֣וּם אֶל־שָׁא֑וּל וְשָׁא֛וּל קָ֥ם מֵהַמְּעָרָ֖ה וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃ס
records.gloss: And restrained David his men with words and not he permitted them to rise against Saul. And Saul arose from the cave and went on [his] way.
pieces: With these words David held his men back and would not let them attack Saul. Saul got up, left the cave and went on his way.

L.8: And David held back his men with [these] words, and did not permit them to rise against Saul. And Saul rose up from the cave and went on [his] way.

R.8: David spoke firmly to his men and did not let them attack Saul. Then Saul got up, left the cave and went on his way.

decisions.choice: restrained: checked them sharply
decisions.reason: The verb elsewhere means to tear apart (Judges 14:6, of Samson tearing the lion). Used of words, it means David cut his men short and held them back with a firm rebuke.

decisions.choice: rise against Saul: attack him
decisions.reason: To rise against someone is to attack (Deuteronomy 19:11; 22:26).

decisions.choice: held back (Balanced); spoke firmly to (Readable)
decisions.reason: Both levels keep the force of the verb: David did not merely advise his men but stopped them with what he said.

records.source: וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֜ד אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן וַיֵּצֵא֙ מֵֽהַמְּעָרָ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֧א אַֽחֲרֵי־שָׁא֛וּל לֵאמֹ֖ר אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּבֵּ֤ט שָׁאוּל֙ אַֽחֲרָ֔יו וַיִּקֹּ֨ד דָּוִ֥ד אַפַּ֛יִם אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And arose David after thus and went out from the cave and called after Saul, saying, My lord the king! And looked Saul behind him, and bowed David face to [the] ground and prostrated himself.
pieces: Afterward David also got up, went out of the cave and called after Saul, "My lord the king!" Saul looked back, and David bowed low with his face to the ground and lay prostrate before him.

L.9: And David arose afterward and went out of the cave and called after Saul, saying, "My lord the king!" And Saul looked behind him, and David bowed his face to the ground and prostrated himself.

R.9: After that, David also came out of the cave. He called after Saul, "My lord the king!" Saul turned to look, and David bowed down low with his face to the ground.

decisions.choice: from the cave: a spelling difference only
decisions.reason: The written text and the form the scribes marked to be read aloud spell "from the cave" slightly differently. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: bowed his face to the ground and prostrated himself: full homage to the king
decisions.reason: Two verbs describe one act of deep respect: bending low and then lying face down (Genesis 43:28; 1 Kings 1:31). David, whom Saul is hunting, still honors him as his king and lord.

decisions.choice: My lord the king
decisions.reason: All levels keep "lord" here, since this is the way a subject addressed a king; Readable keeps it because it is a cry of address, not a description as in verse 7.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ לְשָׁא֔וּל לָ֧מָּה תִשְׁמַ֛ע אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י אָדָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה דָוִ֔ד מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ רָעָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And said David to Saul, Why do you listen to [the] words of man, saying, Look, David [is] seeking your harm?
pieces: David said to Saul, "Why do you listen when {{gender:people|men}} say, 'David is out to harm you'?

L.10: And David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to the words of {{gender:people|men}} who say, 'Look, David seeks your harm'?

R.10: David said to Saul, "Why do you believe {{gender:people|men}} who tell you, 'David wants to hurt you'?

decisions.choice: man: people in general
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being, used here of people as a group. David does not name anyone; he lays the blame on the talk around Saul rather than on Saul himself. Saul had complained that no one told him the truth about David (22:8), and informers had been bringing him reports (23:19).

decisions.choice: seeking your harm: trying to do you evil
decisions.reason: The word means harm or evil. The charge is that David is plotting against the king's life, the charge Saul made in 22:8, 13.

decisions.choice: people (default); men (alternative)
decisions.reason: The word means people of either sex, so every level uses the gender setting. Readable says "believe" for "listen to", since Saul has acted on what he heard.

records.source: הִנֵּה֩ הַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה רָא֣וּ עֵינֶ֗יךָ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־נְתָנְךָ֩ יְהוָ֨ה׀הַיּ֤וֹם׀בְּיָדִי֙ בַּמְּעָרָ֔ה וְאָמַ֥ר לַהֲרָגֲךָ֖ וַתָּ֣חָס עָלֶ֑יךָ וָאֹמַ֗ר לֹא־אֶשְׁלַ֤ח יָדִי֙ בַּֽאדֹנִ֔י כִּי־מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: Look, this day have seen your eyes how gave you [the] LORD today into my hand in the cave. And [one] said to kill you, but it spared you, and I said, Not I will stretch out my hand against my lord, for [the] anointed of [the] LORD [is] he.
pieces: Today you have seen with your own eyes how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put you into my hands in the cave. I was urged to kill you, but I spared you. I said, 'I will not raise my hand against my lord, because he is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed.'

L.11: Look, this day your eyes have seen how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave you today into my hand in the cave. And [someone] said to kill you, but [my eye] spared you, and I said, 'I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, for he is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed.'

R.11: Today you have seen for yourself that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put you in my power in that cave. Some of my men told me to kill you, but I would not. I said, 'I will not attack my master, because he is the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed.'

decisions.choice: and one said to kill you: I was urged to kill you
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject: "someone said", that is, it was said. It points back to David's men urging him in verse 5.

decisions.choice: it spared you: my eye had pity on you, I spared you
decisions.reason: The verb "spare" or "pity" has a feminine subject that is not stated. In this verb's idiom the eye is the one that pities or spares (Deuteronomy 7:16; Ezekiel 7:4), so the sense is "my eye spared you", that is, I spared you. Some old translations read the verb as "I spared"; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the LORD's anointed
decisions.reason: As in verse 7: the king whom the LORD chose and set apart. David repeats to Saul the very words he said to his men.

decisions.choice: I was urged (Balanced); Some of my men told me (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the impersonal "one said" into a passive. Readable names the speakers from verse 5, where it is David's men who urge him. Readable says "in my power" for "into my hand" and "master" and "the king the LORD has anointed" as in verse 7.

records.source: וְאָבִ֣י רְאֵ֔ה גַּ֗ם רְאֵ֛ה אֶת־כְּנַ֥ף מְעִילְךָ֖ בְּיָדִ֑י כִּ֡י בְּכָרְתִי֩ אֶת־כְּנַ֨ף מְעִֽילְךָ֜ וְלֹ֣א הֲרַגְתִּ֗יךָ דַּ֤ע וּרְאֵה֙ כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין בְּיָדִ֜י רָעָ֤ה וָפֶ֨שַׁע֙ וְלֹא־חָטָ֣אתִי לָ֔ךְ וְאַתָּ֛ה צֹדֶ֥ה אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֖י לְקַחְתָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And my father, see, yes, see [the] corner of your robe in my hand, for in my cutting off [the] corner of your robe and not I killed you, know and see that there is not in my hand evil or rebellion, and not I have sinned against you, but you [are] hunting my life to take it.
pieces: My father, look! See the corner of your robe here in my hand! I cut off the corner of your robe, but I did not kill you. You can know for certain from this that I mean you no harm and am not rebelling against you. I have not wronged you, yet you are hunting me down to take my life.

L.12: And my father, see, yes, see the corner of your robe in my hand. For when I cut off the corner of your robe, I did not kill you. Know and see that there is no evil or rebellion in my hand, and I have not sinned against you, yet you are hunting my life to take it.

R.12: My father, look! See this piece of your robe in my hand? I cut it off, but I did not kill you. This proves that I am not trying to hurt you or turn against you. I have done nothing wrong to you, but you are hunting me down to kill me.

decisions.choice: my father: a title of respect, and Saul is also David's father-in-law
decisions.reason: "Father" can address an older man of rank (2 Kings 5:13), and Saul had given his daughter Michal to David as his wife (18:27). David speaks to him as a son, and Saul answers "my son" in verse 17.

decisions.choice: evil or rebellion: harm against the king or a revolt against his rule
decisions.reason: The second word means breaking faith with or rebelling against an authority (1 Kings 12:19). David says that nothing in his hand, that is, nothing in his actions, shows a plan to harm Saul or seize power.

decisions.choice: hunting my life: lying in wait to kill me
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a hunter lying in wait for prey (Exodus 21:13). David uses the same picture of a hunt in 26:20.

decisions.choice: Look ... look (Balanced); look! See ...? (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "see" for emphasis. Balanced keeps the repetition; Readable makes the second a question, which holds the same urgency. Both split the long sentence into several.

records.source: יִשְׁפֹּ֤ט יְהוָה֙ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֔ךָ וּנְקָמַ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה מִמֶּ֑ךָּ וְיָדִ֖י לֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶה־בָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: May judge [the] LORD between me and you, and may avenge me [the] LORD on you, but my hand will not be against you.
pieces: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} judge between us, and may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} avenge the wrong you have done me. But I will not lift my hand against you.

L.13: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} judge between me and you, and may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} avenge me on you, but my hand will not be against you.

R.13: Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} decide which of us is right. Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pay you back for what you have done to me. But I will never harm you myself.

decisions.choice: may the LORD judge and avenge: David leaves justice to God
decisions.reason: David asks God to decide between them and to right the wrong done to him, and he refuses to take that right into his own hands (Deuteronomy 32:35). The same trust is the point of Abigail's words in 25:26, 31-33 and of David's in 26:10.

decisions.choice: my hand will not be against you: I will not harm you
decisions.reason: The hand stands for action and power: David will do Saul no harm himself.

decisions.choice: avenge the wrong you have done me (Balanced); pay you back (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Avenge me on you" means to give David justice by punishing Saul's wrong. Balanced names the wrong to be avenged, and Readable says "pay you back".

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֹאמַ֗ר מְשַׁל֙ הַקַּדְמֹנִ֔י מֵרְשָׁעִ֖ים יֵ֣צֵא רֶ֑שַׁע וְיָדִ֖י לֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶה־בָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: As says [the] proverb of the ancient [ones], From wicked [ones] comes out wickedness, but my hand will not be against you.
pieces: As the old proverb says, 'Wickedness comes from the wicked.' But my hand will not be against you.

L.14: As the proverb of the ancients says, 'From the wicked comes forth wickedness,' but my hand will not be against you.

R.14: There is an old saying: 'Evil things come from evil people.' But I will not harm you.

decisions.choice: the proverb of the ancients: an old saying
alternatives: the proverb of the ancient one (singular)
decisions.reason: The word for proverb is used of a short, well-known saying (10:12). "The ancient ones" may mean people of long ago or simply that the saying is old; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: wickedness comes from the wicked, but my hand will not be against you
alternatives: so my hand will not be against you
decisions.reason: The proverb says that evil deeds come from evil people. David applies it to himself: if he were wicked, he would have killed Saul in the cave; since he did not, Saul can see he is not. It may also hint that Saul's own deeds show what he is, and that God will deal with that. The joining word can be read as "but" or "so".

decisions.choice: an old saying; I will not harm you
decisions.reason: Readable says "saying" for "proverb" and gives the meaning of "my hand will not be against you" as in verse 13.

records.source: אַחֲרֵ֨י מִ֤י יָצָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֥י מִ֖י אַתָּ֣ה רֹדֵ֑ף אַֽחֲרֵי֙ כֶּ֣לֶב מֵ֔ת אַחֲרֵ֖י פַּרְעֹ֥שׁ אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: After whom has come out [the] king of Israel? After whom [are] you pursuing? After a dog dead, after a flea one!
pieces: Whom has the king of Israel come out to chase? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog! A single flea!

L.15: After whom has the king of Israel come out? After whom are you pursuing? After a dead dog! After a single flea!

R.15: Who is the king of Israel chasing? Who are you running after? I am no more important than a dead dog or a tiny flea!

decisions.choice: a dead dog, a single flea: someone of no importance
decisions.reason: To call oneself a dead dog is to say one is worthless and harmless (2 Samuel 9:8; 16:9). A flea is tiny and hard to catch, and it is not worth the chase. David uses the same picture of the flea in 26:20. He is telling Saul that it is beneath a king to pursue him with an army.

decisions.choice: the king of Israel has come out: has marched out to war
decisions.reason: To "come out" is used of a king going out to battle (8:20). Saul has come with 3,000 picked men (verse 3) to hunt one man.

decisions.choice: I am no more important than
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the comparison, which the Hebrew leaves to the hearer.

records.source: וְהָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְדַיָּ֔ן וְשָׁפַ֖ט בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ וְיֵ֨רֶא֙ וְיָרֵ֣ב אֶת־רִיבִ֔י וְיִשְׁפְּטֵ֖נִי מִיָּדֶֽךָ׃פ
records.gloss: And may be [the] LORD as judge and judge between me and you, and may he see and plead my case and vindicate me from your hand.
pieces: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be the judge and decide between you and me. May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} see this, take up my case and rescue me from your power by giving me justice."

L.16: And may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be judge and judge between me and you, and may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} see and plead my case and vindicate me from your hand."

R.16: Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be the judge between you and me. He will see what is right. He will stand up for me and save me from you."

decisions.choice: be judge and judge: decide the case
decisions.reason: The first word is the noun for a judge in a court; the second is the verb. David puts his quarrel with Saul before God as before a court.

decisions.choice: plead my case: act as my defender
decisions.reason: The verb means to argue a legal case (Psalm 43:1; Micah 7:9). God is both the judge and the one who takes David's side.

decisions.choice: judge me from your hand: give me justice by rescuing me from your power
decisions.reason: Here "judge" with "from your hand" means to do justice for someone by delivering them (2 Samuel 18:19, 31). It looks both to God's verdict and to his rescue.

decisions.choice: rescue me from your power by giving me justice (Balanced); save me from you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out the two sides of the verb; Readable keeps the rescue and leaves the justice to the earlier sentences. Readable writes "He" at the start of its sentences, as the style does for every pronoun for God that begins a sentence.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀כְּכַלּ֣וֹת דָּוִ֗ד לְדַבֵּ֞ר אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל הֲקֹלְךָ֥ זֶ֖ה בְּנִ֣י דָוִ֑ד וַיִּשָּׂ֥א שָׁא֛וּל קֹל֖וֹ וַיֵּֽבְךְּ׃
records.gloss: And it was when finished David to speak these words to Saul, and said Saul, [Is] this your voice, my son David? And lifted up Saul his voice and wept.
pieces: When David had finished saying this to Saul, Saul said, "Is that your voice, David my son?" And Saul wept aloud.

L.17: And it happened, when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, that Saul said, "Is this your voice, my son David?" And Saul lifted up his voice and wept.

R.17: When David finished speaking, Saul asked, "Is that you, David, my son?" Then Saul cried loudly.

decisions.choice: is this your voice: Saul recognizes David at a distance
decisions.reason: David is calling from some way off (verse 9; compare 26:13-14, 17, where the same question is asked). Saul knows the voice before he can be sure of the man.

decisions.choice: lifted up his voice and wept: wept aloud
decisions.reason: To lift up the voice and weep is to cry out loud in grief (11:4; Genesis 29:11). Saul is overcome by what David has done and said.

decisions.choice: my son: an answer to "my father"
decisions.reason: Saul answers David's "my father" (verse 12) in the same terms; David is his son-in-law.

decisions.choice: Is that you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the question, whether this is really David, rather than the picture of the voice.

records.heading: Saul admits that David is in the right

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד צַדִּ֥יק אַתָּ֖ה מִמֶּ֑נִּי כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ גְּמַלְתַּ֣נִי הַטּוֹבָ֔ה וַאֲנִ֖י גְּמַלְתִּ֥יךָ הָרָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to David, Righteous [are] you more than I, for you have repaid me the good, and I have repaid you the evil.
pieces: He said to David, "You are more righteous than I am. You have repaid me with good, while I have repaid you with evil.

L.18: And he said to David, "You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me good, and I have repaid you evil.

R.18: He said to David, "You are more righteous than I am. You have been good to me, but I have done bad things to you.

decisions.choice: more righteous than I: more in the right than I
decisions.reason: The word can mean in the right in a dispute (Genesis 38:26, where Judah says the same of Tamar) as well as upright in conduct. Saul admits that David is in the right and he himself in the wrong.

decisions.choice: repaid: dealt out to
decisions.reason: The verb means to deal out or to do to someone, often in return for something. Saul sets his own conduct against David's: good on one side, evil on the other.

decisions.choice: You have been good to me, but I have done bad things to you
decisions.reason: Readable puts "repaid good ... repaid evil" in everyday words and keeps "righteous" as the settled word.

records.source: וְאַתָּה֙ הִגַּ֣דְתָּ הַיּ֔וֹם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֥יתָה אִתִּ֖י טוֹבָ֑ה אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר סִגְּרַ֧נִי יְהוָ֛ה בְּיָדְךָ֖ וְלֹ֥א הֲרַגְתָּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And you have shown today how you have done with me good, how delivered me [the] LORD into your hand and not you killed me.
pieces: Today you have shown how well you have treated me: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} handed me over to you, and you did not kill me.

L.19: And you have shown today how you have dealt well with me, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} delivered me into your hand and you did not kill me.

R.19: Today you showed how kind you have been to me. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} put me in your power, but you did not kill me.

decisions.choice: and you: a spelling difference only
decisions.reason: The written text spells the word "you" in a short form, and the scribes marked the usual form to be read aloud. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: delivered me: shut me up into your hand
decisions.reason: The verb means to shut in or hand over, as a prisoner is handed over (23:11-12, 20). Saul says that God, not chance, put him in David's power.

decisions.choice: you have shown
decisions.reason: The verb means to tell or make known. Saul means that David's actions have made his goodness plain, so the levels say "shown".

records.source: וְכִֽי־יִמְצָ֥א אִישׁ֙ אֶת־אֹ֣יְב֔וֹ וְשִׁלְּח֖וֹ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ טוֹבָ֑ה וַֽיהוָה֙ יְשַׁלֶּמְךָ֣ טוֹבָ֔ה תַּ֚חַת הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתָה לִֽי׃
records.gloss: For if finds a man his enemy, will he send him away on a road good? And [the] LORD may he repay you good in exchange for the day this which you have done to me.
pieces: Who ever finds an enemy and lets him go away unharmed? May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} reward you well for the way you have treated me today.

L.20: For if {{gender:someone|a man}} finds his enemy, will he send him away on a good road? So may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} repay you good for what you have done to me this day.

R.20: People do not find their enemy and then let him go away safe! May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} reward you for what you did for me today.

decisions.choice: if a man finds his enemy, will he send him away safely? A question expecting no
alternatives: a statement: when a man finds his enemy, he will let him go safely only if God moves him to
decisions.reason: The sentence has no question word, but it is best read as a question whose answer is "no one would": no one lets an enemy go when he has him. The point is that what David has done is beyond what anyone would do, and so Saul asks the LORD to reward him.

decisions.choice: on a good road: safely, unharmed
decisions.reason: To send someone on a good way is to let them go in safety.

decisions.choice: in exchange for this day which you have done to me: for what you have done today
decisions.reason: "This day" stands for what happened on it, David's sparing of Saul's life.

decisions.choice: someone (default); a man (alternative)
decisions.reason: The word here is a general "anyone" in a saying about people; Literal uses the gender setting. Balanced and Readable avoid a gendered word for the one who finds the enemy, so they need no setting.

records.source: וְעַתָּה֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י מָלֹ֖ךְ תִּמְל֑וֹךְ וְקָ֨מָה֙ בְּיָ֣דְךָ֔ מַמְלֶ֖כֶת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And now, look, I know that surely you will be king, and will be established in your hand [the] kingdom of Israel.
pieces: Now I know that you will surely become king, and that the kingdom of Israel will be firmly established in your hands.

L.21: And now, look, I know that you will surely be king, and the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hand.

R.21: Now I know for sure that you will be king. You will rule over Israel, and your kingdom will last.

decisions.choice: you will surely be king: the verb is doubled for certainty
decisions.reason: The verb "reign" is repeated, a common way of making a statement emphatic. Saul now says openly what Jonathan had told David (23:17) and what Saul himself had feared (18:8; 20:31).

decisions.choice: the kingdom will be established in your hand: it will stand firm under your rule
decisions.reason: The verb "rise" or "stand" is used of something that lasts and is made secure (13:14, where Saul's kingdom will not stand). Saul says that what was denied to him will be secure in David's hand.

decisions.choice: You will rule over Israel, and your kingdom will last
decisions.reason: Readable divides the sentence and says plainly that David will rule and his kingdom will last.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִשָּׁ֤בְעָה לִּי֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה אִם־תַּכְרִ֥ית אֶת־זַרְעִ֖י אַֽחֲרָ֑י וְאִם־תַּשְׁמִ֥יד אֶת־שְׁמִ֖י מִבֵּ֥ית אָבִֽי׃
records.gloss: And now swear to me by [the] LORD that not you will cut off my offspring after me and that not you will destroy my name from [the] house of my father.
pieces: Now then, give me your oath by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that you will not wipe out my descendants after me or destroy my name from my father's family."

L.22: And now swear to me by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that you will not cut off my offspring after me and that you will not destroy my name from my father's house."

R.22: Now make a promise to me in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Promise that you will not kill off my children and grandchildren after I die. Promise that you will not wipe out my family's name."

decisions.choice: if you will cut off: the form of an oath meaning "that you will not"
decisions.reason: In an oath, "if you do this" leaves a curse unspoken: "may the LORD punish me if I do". So "if you will cut off" means "that you will not cut off".

decisions.choice: cut off offspring, destroy the name: wipe out a family line
decisions.reason: A new king often killed the family of the king before him, so that no heir could claim the throne (1 Kings 15:29; 16:11). A man's name lived on through his descendants; to destroy it was to end his house (Deuteronomy 25:6).

decisions.choice: Jonathan asked the same of David
decisions.reason: Jonathan had made David promise to show faithful love to his family for ever (20:14-17, 42). David keeps both oaths: he cares for Jonathan's son Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9:1-7) and spares him when Saul's descendants are handed over (2 Samuel 21:7).

decisions.choice: children and grandchildren after I die
decisions.reason: Readable explains "my offspring after me" as the family who will live after Saul, and repeats "Promise" to make the two parts of the oath clear.

records.source: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֥ע דָּוִ֖ד לְשָׁא֑וּל וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל־בֵּית֔וֹ וְדָוִד֙ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֔יו עָל֖וּ עַל־הַמְּצוּדָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And swore David to Saul, and went Saul to his house, and David and his men went up to the stronghold.
pieces: So David gave Saul his oath. Then Saul went back home, while David and his men climbed up to the stronghold.

L.23: And David swore to Saul. And Saul went to his house, and David and his men went up to the stronghold.

R.23: So David made that promise to Saul. Then Saul went home. But David and his men went back up to their safe place in the hills.

decisions.choice: the stronghold: David's refuge in the hills
decisions.reason: This is most likely one of the strongholds of En-gedi named in verse 1. David does not go home with Saul; he does not trust that Saul's change of heart will last, and in chapter 26 Saul is hunting him again.

decisions.choice: his house: Saul's home at Gibeah
decisions.reason: Saul's home and royal seat was Gibeah of Benjamin (10:26; 15:34).

decisions.choice: their safe place in the hills
decisions.reason: Readable explains "stronghold" as in verse 1, and adds "back", since David is returning to where he was staying.
